Susan Collins highlights library advocacy and community investments in recent posts
Senator Susan Collins, chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee and representative of Maine, posted a series of messages on social media reflecting on the importance of libraries, community funding, and the legacy of Dolly Parton.
On August 25, 2026, Collins expressed condolences for the death of country music icon Dolly Parton. She wrote, "Saddened to learn of the passing of American icon Dolly Parton. Through the Dollywood Foundation and her global Imagination Library, Dolly gave free books to children around the world, sparking a lifelong love of reading. Her legacy will live on in the classrooms and communities https://t.co/JonRKbrzR2".
The following day, August 26, Collins highlighted her personal connection to libraries and their role in society. She stated, "Libraries have always held a special place in my heart. One of my first jobs as a teenager was reading to children during story hour at the public library in Caribou. Public libraries educate, inspire, and bring communities together. That is why I have worked to secure more than https://t.co/9OaWF9IMK4".
In another post on August 26, she provided information about federal funding secured for local projects across Maine: "Click the link below for an interactive map of the 672 local projects across all 16 Maine counties for which I have secured nearly $1.5 billion in funding through appropriations legislation over the past five years: https://t.co/tGcNH5N6Xv".
Collins draws from a background rooted in her family's lumber business and longstanding public service (official website). She has prioritized initiatives that support sustainable practices in key sectors such as tourism and forestry while also working to improve health care access, education opportunities, small business development, transportation infrastructure, national defense capabilities, and resources for seniors. As chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee with additional roles on committees focused on health and intelligence matters, Collins has directed efforts toward enhancing first responder capabilities and supporting local industries like shipbuilding and manufacturing throughout Maine.
